stories.title: Debbie Pomerantz Launches Independent Multifamily Brokerage
stories.excerpt: Veteran multifamily investment brokerage professional Debbie Pomerantz has launched an independent commercial real estate brokerage firm, DLP Real Estate. The firm’s debut aligns with the $13.25-million sale of Raritan Riverside, a newly constructed, 42-unit luxury multifamily community located at 21 Orlando Dr. in Raritan, NJ. Pomerantz represented the unnamed seller and procured the buyer. The newly completed Raritan Riverside offers a mix of one-bedroom, 1.5-bath and two-bedroom, two-bath modern configurations with high-end appointments and tenant-centric layouts. As part of its lifestyle appeal, the property integrates a newly completed bike path that directly connects residents to the Somerset County Greenway network. “Launching DLP Real Estate allows me to bring a highly agile, creative and unencumbered approach to the multifamily investment sales market,” said Pomerantz, who previously served as SVP with a multifamily-focused brokerage in Northern New Jersey. “Raritan Riverside is the perfect flagship transaction to debut the firm. It represents exactly what today’s apartment-property investors look for: superior architectural visibility that honors its local community while tapping directly into regional lifestyle infrastructure like the Somerset County Greenway.” The post Debbie Pomerantz Launches Independent Multifamily Brokerage appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Debbie Pomerantz launches DLP Real Estate brokerage in Northern New Jersey multifamily market
Raritan Riverside: 42-unit luxury completed asset sells for $13.25M in Raritan, NJ
New bike path connectivity to Somerset County Greenway signals lifestyle amenity demand
stories.summary: Veteran multifamily broker Debbie Pomerantz launched independent brokerage DLP Real Estate, debuting with the $13.25M sale of Raritan Riverside, a newly completed 42-unit luxury property in Raritan, NJ. The property features one- and two-bedroom units with high-end finishes and direct connectivity to regional greenway infrastructure. The transaction signals buyer appetite for well-designed, community-integrated assets in supply-constrained suburban New Jersey submarkets.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development pipeline. This is a brokerage launch and secondary-market asset sale; no supply growth, demand signal, or cost/capital implications for forward development. Northern New Jersey remains a limited-entitlement market with slow new supply, but this transaction alone does not shift underwriting or acquisition strategy.

stories.title: Ambrose Breaks Ground on Buildings at 720-Acre Indiana Business Park
stories.excerpt: Ambrose has broken ground on Buildings I & II at Plainfield Innovation Park, a 720-acre business park in Plainfield, Indiana, a southwest suburb of Indianapolis. Building I will be approximately 181,000 square feet, while Building II will be approximately 217,000 square feet, each including a 2,925-square-foot office area and minimum divisibility of 50,000 square feet. Upon completion, Plainfield Innovation Park will include approximately 14 bulk modern industrial buildings. The groundbreaking follows the announcement of a $138 million investment by Boston Scientific Corporation to develop a new 500,000-square-foot medical device distribution and light manufacturing facility at the park. Ambrose also recently broke ground on the Indianapolis Logistics Park – South, a 16-acre, two-building industrial park in Greenwood, Indiana. The general contractor on Phase I is Compass Commercial Construction Group, with design services provided by ATA Architects. Cushman & Wakefield is handling leasing and marketing for the park, and Ambrose has partnered with Lake City Bank on construction financing. The post Ambrose Breaks Ground on Buildings at 720-Acre Indiana Business Park appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Ambrose breaks ground on Buildings I & II at 720-acre Plainfield Innovation Park, Indianapolis
Boston Scientific $138M investment: 500K SF medical device facility anchors Plainfield Park
Indianapolis Logistics Park–South: 16-acre two-building industrial in nearby Greenwood breaking ground
stories.summary: Ambrose has broken ground on Buildings I and II at Plainfield Innovation Park, a 720-acre business park in Plainfield, Indiana (southwest suburb of Indianapolis), totaling ~398,000 SF of modern industrial space. The groundbreaking follows Boston Scientific's announcement of a $138M investment in a 500,000 SF medical device distribution and light manufacturing facility at the same park. Ambrose is also developing Indianapolis Logistics Park–South in Greenwood with Lake City Bank construction financing.
stories.impact: Massive employer concentration (Boston Scientific + industrial ecosystem) will drive sustained job and population inflow to Indianapolis metro and surrounding suburbs (Plainfield, Greenwood, Carmel corridor), creating strong rental demand for multifamily within 10–20 miles of these logistics nodes. Developers should acquire land and underwrite product (workforce and renter-by-income housing) in nearby residential submarkets before demand capitalization and land prices accelerate; wage growth and employment stability will support rent growth and occupancy resilience.

stories.title: Roscoe Village MF Sells in Deal Brokered by Essex Three-Twelve
stories.excerpt: Essex Three-Twelve completed the sale of 3141 N. Oakley Ave., a turnkey three-unit multifamily property located in Chicago’s Roscoe Village neighborhood. The property sold for $1.24 million, with Essex Three-Twelve Director Mitir Patel representing the seller. Turnkey three-unit properties are rarely available in Roscoe Village, where strong demand and limited inventory continue to create a competitive environment for well-located multifamily assets. Roscoe Village offers access to restaurants and retail, convenient transportation options, and proximity to many of the North Side’s most popular destinations. Essex Three-Twelve generated three offers, including two competing offers, and ultimately secured a full-asking-price offer. “Our goal from the beginning was to maximize the seller’s sale price while strategically exposing the property to the right buyers,” said Patel. “Turnkey three-unit buildings in Roscoe Village don’t become available often, and we knew there would be strong demand.” Stay ahead of the multifamily market at Connect Apartments. Gain firsthand insights from industry leaders on capital markets, development, operations, financing, and investment trends while expanding your network with the people making deals happen. bullets: Essex Three-Twelve sells 3-unit building at 3141 N. Oakley Ave, Chicago's Roscoe Village for $1.24M
Full-asking-price sale; strong demand and limited inventory in tight submarket
Turnkey small multifamily rarely available; competitive bidding drove three offers
stories.summary: Essex Three-Twelve brokered the sale of a turnkey three-unit multifamily property at 3141 N. Oakley Ave in Chicago's Roscoe Village neighborhood for $1.24M at full asking price. The property generated three offers (two competing), reflecting strong renter demand and limited inventory in the North Side submarket. Roscoe Village offers mixed-use walkability, transit access, and proximity to popular neighborhood destinations.
stories.impact: Roscoe Village (and similar Chicago North Side neighborhoods) exhibit classic supply-constrained rental demand dynamics: turnkey small multifamily scarcity, full-ask sales, and competitive buyer interest. Developers should prioritize acquisition and value-add renovation of small aging buildings in these neighborhoods for rent-up; limited new zoning for mid-rise product and competition from owner-occupants create a moat around existing rental supply. Cap-rate compression and buyer competition signal strong rent fundamentals and low turnover risk—justifies higher per-unit acquisition prices and rehab CapEx.

stories.title: Hunneman Named Leasing Agent for Tewksbury Office Complex
stories.excerpt: Hunneman has been appointed as the exclusive leasing agent for Highwood Office Park, a three-building office campus located in Tewksbury, MA, on behalf of KS Partners. The property is comprised of more than 265,000 square feet of office and flex use space across 1, 2 and 3 Highwood Dr., with available suites ranging from approximately 4,000 to 67,000 square feet. The campus has undergone significant renovations in recent years and offers modern amenities, flexible floor plans, and a range of workspace solutions designed to support today’s user types, according to Hunneman. “We’re excited to represent the Highwood Office Park and to reintroduce this exceptional suburban campus opportunity to the marketplace,” said Chris Curley, EVP at Hunneman. “With flexible floor plates, a full amenities package and a strategic location along the I-93 and I-495 corridor, the property has all the “must have” qualities to satisfy the ever-evolving needs of today’s tenants.” The post Hunneman Named Leasing Agent for Tewksbury Office Complex appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Hunneman appointed exclusive leasing agent for Highwood Office Park, Tewksbury, MA
265K SF office/flex space across three buildings; renovated, flexible floor plates
Strategic location I-93/I-495 corridor; office leasing mandate signals suburban demand
stories.summary: Hunneman has been named exclusive leasing agent for Highwood Office Park, a 265,000 SF office and flex-use campus in Tewksbury, MA (on the I-93/I-495 corridor north of Boston). The three-building property, owned by KS Partners, has undergone recent renovations and offers flexible floor plates and modern amenities. Available suites range from 4,000 to 67,000 SF.
stories.impact: Negligible for multifamily development. This is an office/flex leasing mandate, not a residential or mixed-use story. No signal of residential demand, supply, capital availability, or cost implications for apartment development in the Boston suburbs. Suburban office leasing activity does not drive renter demand unless paired with significant employer relocation or headcount growth; this story contains no such indicator.

stories.title: Keystone Arranges $22M Permanent Loan for Belmont Multifamily
stories.excerpt: Keystone recently closed on a $22,000,000 permanent loan on a multifamily property located in Belmont. The financing wasprovided by Voya Financial at a fixed interest rate of 5.47%. The borrower was not disclosed. The transaction reflects continued lender appetite for well-located multifamily assets in supply-constrained California markets, and demonstrates Keystone’s ability to source competitive, long-term institutional financing for its clients, the company said. “We are pleased to have arranged this financing on behalf of our client,” said managing director Nick Viscount at Keystone. “Voyademonstrated a strong commitment to this asset and we were able to deliver a highly competitive structure that met the borrower’s long-term objectives.” Belmont is a sought-after residential submarket situated in San Mateo County on the San Francisco Peninsula. It benefits from strong employment fundamentals, limited housing supply and consistent renter demand driven by proximity to major technology and life sciences employers throughout the Bay Area, according to Keystone. The post Keystone Arranges $22M Permanent Loan for Belmont Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Keystone arranged $22M permanent loan, Voya Financial, 5.47% fixed rate on Belmont multifamily
San Mateo County (Bay Area) supply-constrained market; technology/life sciences employer base
Institutional fixed-rate financing at sub-5.5% signals continued lender appetite for core assets
stories.summary: Keystone closed a $22M permanent loan from Voya Financial at a fixed rate of 5.47% for a multifamily property in Belmont, California (San Mateo County, San Francisco Peninsula). The transaction demonstrates institutional lender commitment to well-located assets in supply-constrained California markets. Belmont benefits from strong employment fundamentals, limited housing supply, and renter demand driven by proximity to Bay Area tech and life sciences employers.
stories.impact: Bay Area multifamily (especially Peninsula submarkets like Belmont) remains a core play for institutional capital despite recent rate environment uncertainty. Fixed-rate permanent financing at 5.47% reflects lender confidence in rent growth, occupancy stability, and employment durability. Developers and investors with existing Bay Area assets or development pipelines should move to lock long-term debt now; spreads remain favorable for supply-constrained markets with strong job growth. Limited new supply and sustained in-migration from tech sector (despite recent corrections) support rent resilience and justify higher basis acquisition and development costs in these submarkets.

stories.title: AI Wealth Management Platform Vise Grabs 12K SF at 50 Ninth Avenue
stories.excerpt: Artificial intelligence-powered wealth management platform Vise is moving from SoHo to 50 Ninth Avenue in the Meatpacking District, where it will quadruple its office space to 11,949 square feet. The space spans the second floor of several combined historic townhomes along the Ninth Avenue frontage and therefore has dramatic, over 20 foot-high pitched ceilings and an atrium outdoor garden. Rob Kluge and Brandon Charnas of Current Real Estate Advisors represented the tenant in the 10-year lease. Howard Hersch, Greg Conen, Jennifer Schreiber and Natalie Serio of Newmark represented the building owner, Tavros Capital, which will build out the space. The asking rent was $150 per square foot. Vise is an AI-driven wealth management platform for independent advisors founded by Samir Vasavada and Runik Mehrotra that launched in November 2019. It hosts over $100 billion in assets and the firm is reported to be valued at over $22 billion. It is currently located in 4,000 square feet of office space at 521 Broadway in SoHo. In searching for new digs, Vise was focused on upgrading both its office and culture. “We worked with ownership on a creative solution whereby the ground-floor retailer, Jen Rubio’s fashion company — now known as Elsa, which was then negotiating their deal — would expand upstairs and take roughly another 4,000 to 5,000 square feet on the West 14th Street side of the floor,” Charnas said. “That allowed us to create a space for Vise that fit both their program and their budget.” “We worked through multiple iterations with ownership and the architect to take what had been one larger floor and create the right long-term home for Vise,” added Kluge. The resulting space primarily overlooks Ninth Avenue and sits directly across from the Apple store, with dramatic vaulted ceilings, tons of light and a build-out being designed specifically around Vise’s needs and specifications. It will also sit above the new Delilah club and across from the planned Annabel’s member
bullets: AI wealth management platform Vise expands from 4K SF SoHo to 11,949 SF Meatpacking District

stories.summary: Artificial intelligence-powered wealth management platform Vise is expanding its NYC office footprint, signing a 10-year lease for 11,949 SF at 50 Ninth Avenue in the Meatpacking District (quadrupling from its current 4,000 SF SoHo space at $150/SF). Vise, valued at $22B+ and hosting $100B in assets under management, relocates to dramatic historic space with 20+ foot ceilings and an atrium garden. Current Real Estate Advisors represented the tenant; Newmark represented owner Tavros Capital.
stories.impact: Minimal direct impact to multifamily development. This is a single office leasing transaction within Manhattan's ongoing office recovery narrative. While Vise's growth and relocation signals fintech expansion in NYC, office tenant activity does not directly drive residential demand or affect multifamily supply, capital, or construction costs. However, tech/fintech talent concentration in Manhattan and Brooklyn (Meatpacking, Williamsburg, DUMBO) continues to support premium renter demand in nearby residential neighborhoods; developers should remain attentive to fintech and AI company clustering as a leading indicator of neighborhood gentrification and rent upside in adjacent multifamily assets.

stories.title: SME Capital Forced to Hand Over Hudson Yards Condo Building to Residents
stories.excerpt: Private investment firm SME Capital Ventures is handing ownership of 441 West 37th Street to the condominium board after an investigation by the New York Attorney General’s office. SME acquired the building out of foreclosure in 2023. It then failed to pay bills related to the Hudson Yards property and neglected safety violations, leading to a settlement to pay $700,000, according to Attorney General Letitia James. Built in 2020 by Levi Balkany, the nine-unit building went into foreclosure in 2023. SME never reported to the state that it was the winning bidder in the auction and never acknowledged that it owned the building, leaving residents to pick up the tab for things like a new $15,824 certificate of occupancy, according to the AG. Some of the units were rented out while awaiting buyers, including 35 formerly homeless people who were ousted around the time SME took control of the building, according to The Real Deal. “Private equity firms do not get to pick and choose which laws apply to them,” James said in a statement. “When this company took control of a Manhattan condo building, it took on real legal responsibilities to the homeowners who lived there. For two years, SME Capital dodged those duties while still collecting rent checks. My office will keep holding these firms accountable when they put profits over New Yorkers’ safety.” Balkany could not be reached for comment. bullets: SME Capital Ventures forfeits 441 W 37th St, Hudson Yards 9-unit condo to board after NY AG settlement
SME acquired building from 2023 foreclosure; unpaid bills, safety violations; $700K penalty
35 formerly homeless residents displaced; failed governance signals distressed asset risk
stories.summary: Private investment firm SME Capital Ventures has handed ownership of a nine-unit condo building at 441 West 37th Street in Hudson Yards back to the condominium board following a New York Attorney General investigation. SME acquired the building out of foreclosure in 2023 but failed to pay bills, maintain building operations, and address safety violations. The settlement required a $700,000 penalty payment; the building had housed 35 formerly homeless individuals who were displaced when SME took control.
stories.impact: Cautionary signal for distressed asset acquisition and foreclosure strategies in NYC multifamily. SME's failure to manage the asset, disclose ownership, and honor tenant/operational obligations triggered regulatory enforcement and loss of equity. For developers and investors: foreclosure acquisitions in NYC remain subject to heightened Attorney General scrutiny around tenant displacement and building maintenance; dark equity plays carry reputational and legal risk. Conversely, this reinforces scarcity of available inventory in prime submarkets like Hudson Yards—distressed condo conversions are few and regulatory barriers are high, protecting existing rental supply and supporting rent growth in competing multifamily assets.

stories.title: Sisters of the Visitation Monastery Sells to Integritas Capital for $42M
stories.excerpt: A 170-year-old monastery in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, has sold for $42.25 million. The Sisters of the Visitation’s 7.5-acre campus at 8902 Ridge Boulevard — a campus behind 30-foot stone walls, with a monastery, chapel and school — was bought by a group of Brooklyn-based developers and investors with a history of large residential projects, including leaders of Integritas Capital and Heights Advisors. A petition by the Catholic religious order to sell its real estate was approved by the office of the New York State Attorney General on Monday. Nonprofits are required by New York law to obtain approval when it sells all or most of its assets. The buyer entity, 1137 91 LLC, is led by Brooklyn real estate investor Stephen Palmese, founder of private equity platform Integritas Capital (and a former vice chair at JLL). Passive investors included Rachel Foster, founder and president of Brooklyn housing developer Heights Advisors, alongside the developer’s director, Scott Geddes, as well as Daniel Kodsi and Matthew Kodsi . The longtime professional partners are planning a resort-residential tower in Fort Lauderdale, according to The Real Deal. Palmese’s Integritas is also the lender behind a forthcoming 27-story church-to-residential conversion in Brooklyn’s Fort Greene. The cohort of buyers suggests the historic property’s likely fate as a major mixed-used or residential development. The Visitation Sisters entered into an initial contract in late April, according to the filing, but the school and monastery have been shuttered since 2024, after their numbers dropped too low to sustain full ministry. The Visitation Sisters, formally the Order of the Visitation of Holy Mary, were a French order founded in 1610. Their presence in Brooklyn dates back to 1855. The sellers expect net proceeds of $40.9 million, according to the filing, which will be held in escrow under an approved dissolution and distribution of assets plan. bullets: Sisters of Visitation Monastery, Bay Ridge Brooklyn, sells 7.5-acre campus for $42.25M to Integritas Capital

stories.summary: The Sisters of the Visitation have sold their 170-year-old, 7.5-acre monastery campus at 8902 Ridge Boulevard in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, for $42.25M to a development consortium led by Integritas Capital founder Stephen Palmese and Heights Advisors' Rachel Foster. The transaction received approval from the New York State Attorney General's office, as required for nonprofit asset dispositions. The site includes a monastery, chapel, school, and is enclosed by 30-foot stone walls on a prominent Bay Ridge location.
stories.impact: Significant land and entitlement opportunity in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn—a historically underinvested outer-borough neighborhood with improving transit connectivity (R train) and growing demand for affordable/workforce housing. A 7.5-acre institutional campus is rare and likely has zoning flexibility (C6 or R7-2 equivalent, potentially eligible for inclusionary/MZTE density bonus). Developers should track this asset for redevelopment timeline and zoning strategy; mixed-use or residential conversion could yield 400–600 units depending on entitlement and building preservation requirements. Bay Ridge's gentrification trajectory is slower than Williamsburg/Park Slope but steady; entry pricing at $42M for 7.5 acres suggests acquisition basis of ~$170/unit equivalent for ~250 units, indicating runway for value creation and long-hold rent growth.

stories.title: Benefit Street Partners Provides $103M Bridge Debt for Texas Multifamily Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Vantage Communities has secured $103 million in bridge debt to refinance a three-property, 864-unit multifamily portfolio in three cities in Texas, Commercial Observer can first report. Benefit Street Partners provided the debt, which will finance the property toward full stabilization and is structured as a floating-rate, interest-only bridge loan with a three-year term. Greystone Capital Advisors‘ Drew Fletcher, Bryan Grover, Jesse Kopecky and Cameron Behr arranged the transaction. “Benefit Street Partners recognized the quality of the sponsorship, the assets, and the long-term fundamentals supporting these dynamic Central Texas markets,” said Fletcher. The three assets are split among Vantage at Hutto — a 288-unit complex located at 1051 North Farm to Market 1660 in Hutto, Tex., just outside of Austin; Vantage at McKinney Falls — a 288-unit complex located at 7900 McKinney Falls Parkway in suburban Austin, Tex.; and Vantage at Fair Oaks — a 288-unit complex located at 9135 Dietz Elkhorn Road in Boerne, Tex. outside of San Antonio. All three assets opened in either 2023 or 2024 and feature amenities such as resident clubhouses, fitness centers and resort-style swimming pools. “We were pleased to structure a financing solution that met our clients’ objectives while leveraging the strength of this high-quality, recently delivered portfolio,” added Fletcher in a statement. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Benefit Street Partners provides $103M bridge debt to Vantage Communities for 3-property, 864-unit Texas portfolio
Three assets: Hutto (288 units), McKinney Falls (288 units), Fair Oaks (288 units); all Austin-area
Floating-rate, interest-only, three-year bridge; Greystone Capital arranged; targets full stabilization
stories.summary: Vantage Communities has secured $103M in floating-rate, interest-only bridge debt from Benefit Street Partners to refinance a three-property, 864-unit multifamily portfolio across Central Texas: Vantage at Hutto (288 units), Vantage at McKinney Falls (288 units, suburban Austin), and Vantage at Fair Oaks (288 units, Boerne, TX). Greystone Capital Advisors arranged the transaction. The bridge has a three-year term and is structured to finance the properties toward stabilization.
stories.impact: Floating-rate bridge debt ($103M across 864 units = ~$119K/unit) signals strong sponsor and asset-level underwriting in Austin metro and greater Central Texas region. Bridge debt availability reflects robust market fundamentals (employment growth, rent momentum, low vacancy) that support floating-rate risk. Austin's population influx (tech, remote work, migration from coastal metros) continues to drive renter demand; multiple bridge refinancings in the metro signal that value-add/stabilization plays are generating returns and attracting institutional capital. Developers with land or pre-development assets in Austin, Round Rock, Pflugerville, Hutto, and Boerne submarkets should accelerate starts—cap rates remain compressed and take-out financing is available, but construction costs and land basis continue to escalate. Competition for land parcels is intense; timing is critical for acquisition ahead of 2024–2025 price escalation.

stories.title: Coastland Residential Lands $85M to Build Miami-Dade Rental
stories.excerpt: Coastland Residential has nabbed a $84.5 million construction loan for a multifamily development near Tropical Park in southwest Miami-Dade County. The debt from PNC Bank covers the Vybe 75, which will house 366 apartments and 5,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space. The eight-story development at 4383 Southwest 75th Avenue sits just east of Tropical Park and the Palmetto Expressway, south of Bird Road. At least a portion of the units will be priced within 120 percent of the area’s median income, though a representative for the Pinecrest-based developer declined to provide an exact figure. Amenities will include a rooftop pool, a gym, a co-working lounge, a sports simulator and a movie theater. Coastland Residential purchased the 4.3-acre site for $14.5 million last year, according to property records. The Corwil Architects-designed development represents the first phase of a larger project that’s expected to deliver about 1,000 units in total. Launched five years ago by Anthony Seijas and Alejandro Rodriguez, Coastland Residential grew out of Rodriguez’s contracting and construction management firm, Coastland Construction, which is also serving as the contractor for Vybe 75. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Coastland Residential secures $84.5M construction loan from PNC Bank for Vybe 75 in southwest Miami-Dade
366-unit eight-story development + 5K SF retail at 4383 SW 75th Ave, near Tropical Park, Pinecrest
Affordable component: units at 120% AMI; Phase 1 of larger 1K-unit project; land acquired for $14.5M
stories.summary: Coastland Residential has obtained an $84.5M construction loan from PNC Bank for Vybe 75, a 366-unit, eight-story multifamily development with 5,000 SF of ground-floor retail in southwest Miami-Dade County near Tropical Park and the Palmetto Expressway. At least a portion of units will be priced at up to 120% of area median income. The Corwil Architects-designed project represents Phase 1 of a larger buildout expected to deliver ~1,000 total units; the developer (Coastland Residential, founded five years ago by Anthony Seijas and Alejandro Gutierrez) acquired the 4.3-acre site in 2023 for $14.5M.
stories.impact: Miami-Dade continued supply growth and PNC lending availability signal sustained developer confidence in South Florida rental demand despite recent market cooling and inventory buildup in core Miami subsets. Vybe 75's workforce/affordable-skewing component (120% AMI units) and Phase 1/Phase 2 phasing strategy hedge against near-term oversupply risk; affordability positioning will attract institutional and tax-credit financing. However, Coastland's acquisition basis of ~$40/SF on raw land ($14.5M / 4.3 acres) and project density (~85 units/acre across full 1K buildout) suggests builders are repricing basis downward to reflect recent construction cost inflation and cap-rate expansion. Developers should model Miami-Dade projects conservatively (assume 4.75–5.25% exit cap rates, 5–6% construction cost escalation, extended lease-up); Phase 1/Phase 2 phasing provides flexibility to pause/adjust if market deteriorates in 2024–2025.
